output.title: Enterprise Customer Management Application (CMA) Requirements
output.summary: A web-based customer management application for storing, searching, and maintaining customer, contact, and interaction data. Backend: Java (Spring Boot, REST API). Frontend: React (TypeScript SPA). Data store: PostgreSQL. Delivered to enterprise standards for security, auditability, availability, accessibility, observability, and maintainability, with role-based access and privacy-regulation support (e.g., GDPR).

functional_requirements.title: Customer record creation
functional_requirements.description: Authorized users can create customer records (individual or organization) with name, type, status, industry, tax/registration ID, and notes, plus multiple addresses, emails, and phone numbers.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Valid submission persists the record and returns a unique ID; invalid or missing mandatory fields are rejected with field-level error messages.

functional_requirements.title: Customer record view and edit
functional_requirements.description: Users can view and edit customer details, with optimistic locking to prevent lost updates from concurrent edits.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Edits persist and display immediately; a stale-version update is rejected with a conflict message and no data is overwritten.

functional_requirements.title: Customer deactivation and deletion
functional_requirements.description: Customers are soft-deleted (archived) by default; authorized administrators can restore archived records or permanently erase them per retention and privacy rules.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Archived customers are hidden from default lists, restorable by admins, and permanent erasure removes personal data while retaining anonymized audit entries.

functional_requirements.title: Search, filter, and sort
functional_requirements.description: Users can search by name, ID, email, phone, and address, filter by status, type, owner, and tags, and sort and paginate results server-side.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Search over 1M records returns the first page within the performance target; filters combine correctly; pagination is stable.

functional_requirements.title: Contact management
functional_requirements.description: Each organization customer can have multiple contacts with roles and a designated primary contact.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Contacts can be added, edited, and removed; exactly one primary contact is enforced per customer.

functional_requirements.title: Interaction and notes log
functional_requirements.description: Users can record interactions (calls, meetings, emails, notes) against a customer, with timestamp, author, and type, displayed in a chronological timeline.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Entries appear in the timeline in order, show author and time, and can only be edited or deleted by the author or an admin.

functional_requirements.title: Authentication and SSO
functional_requirements.description: Users authenticate via the enterprise identity provider using OIDC/SAML with MFA enforced by the IdP; sessions use short-lived tokens with refresh.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Unauthenticated requests receive 401; expired tokens are refreshed or the user is redirected to login; logout invalidates the session.

functional_requirements.title: Role-based access control
functional_requirements.description: Roles (Admin, Manager, Agent, Read-Only) control permissions at the API and UI level, including optional record ownership scoping.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Unauthorized actions return 403 at the API and are hidden in the UI; permissions are verified by automated tests for every role.

functional_requirements.title: Audit trail
functional_requirements.description: All create, update, delete, export, and access-to-sensitive-data events are recorded with actor, timestamp, action, and before/after values, and are viewable by auditors.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Every mutating action produces an immutable audit entry; audit entries cannot be modified or deleted via the application.

functional_requirements.title: Import and export
functional_requirements.description: Authorized users can bulk import customers from CSV with validation and a preview, and export search results to CSV.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Import reports row-level errors without partial commit of invalid files; exports respect the user's permissions and are audited.

functional_requirements.title: Duplicate detection and merge
functional_requirements.description: The system flags probable duplicates on create and import and lets authorized users merge records, preserving history.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Potential duplicates are shown before save; a merge retains all contacts and interactions and records an audit entry.

functional_requirements.title: Privacy and data subject requests
functional_requirements.description: Support consent tracking, data subject access export, rectification, and erasure of an individual's personal data.
functional_requirements.acceptance: A subject's data can be exported in a machine-readable format and erased on request within the defined workflow, with the action audited.

functional_requirements.title: Tags and custom fields
functional_requirements.description: Admins can define tags and a limited set of custom fields for customer records.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Custom fields appear in forms, search filters, and exports with type validation.

functional_requirements.title: REST API and documentation
functional_requirements.description: All functionality is exposed through a versioned REST API documented with OpenAPI.
functional_requirements.acceptance: The OpenAPI spec is generated and published, and the UI consumes only this API.

functional_requirements.title: Administration console
functional_requirements.description: Admins can manage users' role assignments, reference data (statuses, types), and view system health and audit logs.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Admin changes take effect without redeployment and are audited.

non_functional_requirements.description: 95th percentile API response under 500 ms for reads and 1 s for writes at 200 concurrent users; search page loads in under 2 s on a dataset of 1M customers.
99.9% monthly availability, with zero-downtime deployments and health/readiness endpoints.

Comply with OWASP ASVS Level 2: TLS 1.2+ in transit, encryption at rest, parameterized queries, input validation, CSRF/XSS protection, secure headers, secrets in a vault, and dependency vulnerability scanning in CI.
Meet GDPR (and applicable local) requirements, including data minimization, retention rules, field-level protection of sensitive PII, and data residency as determined by the organization.
Stateless backend that scales horizontally; database supports read replicas and indexed queries for expected growth to 5M customers.
Automated daily backups with point-in-time recovery; RPO of 15 minutes or less and RTO of 4 hours or less, with restore tested at least quarterly.
Structured logging with correlation IDs, metrics, distributed tracing, and alerting on error rates and latency; no PII in logs.
The UI conforms to WCAG 2.2 AA, is responsive, and supports current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari.

At least 80% automated unit test coverage on business logic, plus integration tests (Testcontainers with PostgreSQL), API contract tests, and end-to-end tests of critical flows; static analysis gates in CI.

Containerized services delivered through a CI/CD pipeline with infrastructure as code, versioned database migrations (Flyway or Liquibase), and separate dev, test, staging, and production environments.
UI text externalized for localization; dates, times, and numbers are locale-aware; timestamps stored in UTC.

constraints.description: Backend must be implemented in Java (LTS version 21 or later) using a mainstream framework such as Spring Boot.
Frontend must be implemented in React.
PostgreSQL (a currently supported major version) is the system of record.
Solution must integrate with the organization's existing identity provider and approved hosting platform.
Only open-source or organization-approved licensed libraries may be used, subject to license and vulnerability review.

assumptions.description: An enterprise OIDC/SAML identity provider with MFA is available for integration.
Customers include both individuals and organizations (B2B and B2C).
Expected scale is up to 5M customer records and about 500 named users, with 200 concurrent.
Deployment targets a containerized environment (Kubernetes or equivalent) in a cloud or on-premises data center.
The application is for internal staff use, not a customer self-service portal.
English is the initial UI language, with other locales added later.

open_decisions.question: Which backend architecture style should be used?
open_decisions.recommended: Modular monolith
open_decisions.impact: Affects delivery speed, operational complexity, and future scalability; a modular monolith can be split later.

open_decisions.question: Which regulatory regimes apply and where must data reside?
options: GDPR plus other regional laws (e.g., CCPA)
open_decisions.recommended: GDPR plus other regional laws (e.g., CCPA)
open_decisions.impact: Drives erasure, consent, retention, hosting region, and audit design.

open_decisions.question: How should full-text customer search be implemented?
open_decisions.recommended: PostgreSQL full-text and trigram indexes
open_decisions.impact: Dedicated engine adds infrastructure and sync complexity; Postgres suffices for the stated scale.

open_decisions.question: Should integrations with other systems (CRM, ERP, email, notifications) be in the first release?
open_decisions.recommended: Outbound webhooks/events only
open_decisions.impact: Affects scope, schedule, and data model; events keep later integration open.

open_decisions.question: What data retention periods apply to archived customers, interactions, and audit logs?
options: Defined by legal and records management
open_decisions.recommended: Defined by legal and records management
open_decisions.impact: Determines purge jobs, storage sizing, and compliance exposure.

open_decisions.question: Which hosting platform and deployment model will be used?
options: Public cloud managed Kubernetes and managed PostgreSQL
open_decisions.recommended: Public cloud managed Kubernetes and managed PostgreSQL
open_decisions.impact: Affects operations effort, availability, backup tooling, and cost.

acceptance_criteria.description: A user with the Agent role can create, edit, and archive a customer, and every action appears in the audit trail with correct actor and values.
Two users editing the same record concurrently cannot silently overwrite each other; the second save receives a conflict response.
On a 1M-record dataset, search and filter return the first page within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile under 200 concurrent users.
Role permission matrix tests confirm each role can perform only its permitted operations at both API and UI levels, and unauthenticated access is denied.
A data subject access request produces a complete export, and an erasure request removes personal data while preserving anonymized audit records.
A CSV import with invalid rows is rejected with row-level errors and no partial data committed; a valid file imports and is audited.
The security pipeline reports no unresolved critical or high vulnerabilities, and penetration testing against OWASP ASVS L2 passes before release.
Automated accessibility scans and manual checks show WCAG 2.2 AA conformance on core workflows.
A restore from backup to a point in time meets the RPO and RTO targets in a rehearsal, and a rolling deployment completes with no user-visible downtime.
The published OpenAPI specification matches implemented endpoints, and contract tests pass in CI.
Logs and traces contain correlation IDs and no personal data, and alerts fire when error-rate or latency thresholds are breached.

out_of_scope: Customer self-service portal or public-facing access
Marketing automation, campaign management, and email sending
Sales pipeline, quoting, invoicing, and billing
Native mobile applications
Advanced analytics, BI dashboards, and AI-based features
Integrations with specific third-party CRM/ERP systems in the first release (pending OD-004)
Data migration from legacy systems beyond CSV import

output.title: Enterprise Customer Management Application (Java, React, PostgreSQL)
output.summary: A web-based customer management application that lets authorised staff create, view, search, update, segment and deactivate customer records, manage contacts, addresses and notes, and import/export data. The backend is a Java REST service, the frontend is a React single-page application, and PostgreSQL is the system of record. The solution must meet enterprise standards for security, auditability, privacy compliance, availability, performance, observability, testing and operability.

functional_requirements.title: Customer record creation
functional_requirements.description: Authorised users can create a customer (individual or organisation) with mandatory fields (type, legal/display name, status) and optional fields (industry, tax/registration ID, website, tags, account owner). The system assigns a unique, immutable customer number.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Given valid input, a customer is created and returned with a unique customer number; invalid or missing mandatory fields return field-level validation errors and nothing is persisted.

functional_requirements.title: Customer view and edit
functional_requirements.description: Users can view a full customer profile and edit permitted fields. Concurrent edits are detected and not silently overwritten.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Edits are persisted and visible immediately; a stale update (outdated version) is rejected with a conflict response and the user is prompted to reload.

functional_requirements.title: Contacts management
functional_requirements.description: Each customer can have multiple contacts (name, role, email, phone, preferred channel) with one designated primary contact.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Contacts can be added, edited and removed; exactly one primary contact is enforced per customer; email and phone formats are validated.

functional_requirements.title: Address management
functional_requirements.description: Each customer can have multiple typed addresses (billing, shipping, registered) with country-aware validation.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Addresses can be added, edited and removed; required fields vary by country; at most one default per address type.

functional_requirements.title: Search, filter and sort
functional_requirements.description: Users can search customers by name, customer number, email, phone and tags, and filter by status, type, owner, segment and created/updated date, with sortable, paginated results.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Search returns correct paginated results with total count; partial and case-insensitive matches work; filters combine with AND logic; page size is capped server-side.

functional_requirements.title: Notes and activity timeline
functional_requirements.description: Users can add notes and see a chronological timeline of notes and key changes (status change, owner change, contact changes) per customer.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Notes record author and timestamp, are immutable apart from author/admin edit with history, and appear in the timeline in order.

functional_requirements.title: Status lifecycle and deactivation
functional_requirements.description: Customers move through defined statuses (e.g. Prospect, Active, Inactive, Archived). Deletion is soft by default; restoration is possible by permitted roles.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Only allowed transitions succeed; deactivated customers are excluded from default searches; restore returns the customer to its prior status with an audit entry.

functional_requirements.title: Duplicate detection
functional_requirements.description: On create and edit, the system warns about probable duplicates (matching tax ID, email or fuzzy name/address match) and supports merging two customers by authorised users.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Probable duplicates are displayed before save; a merge consolidates contacts, addresses and notes into a surviving record and retains a merge audit trail.

functional_requirements.title: Authentication and SSO
functional_requirements.description: Users authenticate through the enterprise identity provider using OpenID Connect/OAuth 2.0 with MFA enforced by the IdP; API access uses short-lived tokens.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Unauthenticated requests receive 401; expired tokens are rejected; successful login maps IdP claims to application roles.

functional_requirements.title: Role-based access control
functional_requirements.description: Access is governed by roles (e.g. Viewer, Agent, Manager, Administrator) with permissions enforced server-side, optionally scoped by team or region.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Each role can perform only its permitted operations; unauthorised calls return 403 regardless of UI state; permission matrix is covered by automated tests.

functional_requirements.title: Audit logging
functional_requirements.description: All create, update, delete, restore, merge, export, login and permission-change events are recorded with actor, timestamp, source IP, entity and before/after values.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Audit entries are generated for every listed event, cannot be edited or deleted via the application, and are searchable by authorised auditors.

functional_requirements.title: Bulk import
functional_requirements.description: Administrators can import customers from CSV/XLSX with a validation preview, error report and the option to commit only valid rows.
functional_requirements.acceptance: A file of up to the configured limit is validated asynchronously; a downloadable error report lists row-level errors; committed imports are atomic per batch and audited.

functional_requirements.title: Export
functional_requirements.description: Authorised users can export filtered customer lists to CSV/XLSX, with fields limited by role.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Export reflects current filters and the user's field permissions; large exports run asynchronously; every export is audited.

functional_requirements.title: Segments and tags
functional_requirements.description: Users can tag customers and define saved filters (segments) for reuse and sharing.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Tags can be created, applied and removed; saved segments return the same results as the equivalent ad hoc filter.

functional_requirements.title: Data privacy operations
functional_requirements.description: The system supports data subject requests: export of a person's data, rectification, and erasure/anonymisation subject to retention rules, plus consent and marketing preference tracking.
functional_requirements.acceptance: A data subject export contains all personal data held; an erasure request anonymises personal fields while preserving legally required records; consent changes are timestamped and audited.

functional_requirements.title: REST API and documentation
functional_requirements.description: All functionality is exposed through a versioned REST API documented with OpenAPI, consistently using standard error formats and pagination.
functional_requirements.acceptance: A published OpenAPI spec matches the implemented endpoints (verified in CI); errors follow a single problem-details schema; breaking changes require a new API version.

functional_requirements.title: Administration
functional_requirements.description: Administrators can manage users' role assignments, reference data (statuses, industries, countries, tags) and system settings.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Changes take effect without redeployment, are validated and are audited.

functional_requirements.title: Responsive, accessible UI
functional_requirements.description: The React UI provides list, detail, create/edit and admin screens, with clear validation feedback, loading and error states, and keyboard and screen-reader support.
functional_requirements.acceptance: All primary journeys are completable by keyboard only and pass automated accessibility checks with no critical violations; UI works on current desktop and tablet browsers.

non_functional_requirements.description: Comply with OWASP ASVS Level 2: input validation, output encoding, CSRF/XSS/SQL-injection protection, secure headers, rate limiting, and secure session/token handling. Secrets are held in a managed secret store, never in source control.
Encrypt data in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (database, backups and file storage). Sensitive fields (e.g. tax IDs) use additional field-level protection where required by classification.

95th percentile API response time under 500 ms for read/search and under 800 ms for writes at 200 concurrent users with 5 million customer records; initial UI load under 3 s on a standard corporate network.
The backend is stateless and horizontally scalable; the database supports read replicas and indexing strategies sufficient for the stated data volume.
99.9% monthly availability for production, with RPO of 15 minutes or less and RTO of 4 hours or less; zero-downtime deployments.
Automated daily backups with point-in-time recovery, with restore tested at least quarterly. Database schema changes are managed by versioned, repeatable migrations.

Structured logging with correlation IDs, metrics (RED/USE), distributed tracing and health/readiness endpoints; alerts on error rate, latency and saturation. Logs must not contain personal data or credentials.
Layered, modular architecture with automated code style and static analysis; minimum 80% unit test coverage on business logic; architecture decisions recorded as ADRs.
Automated unit, integration (using real PostgreSQL via containers), API contract, end-to-end and security (SAST, dependency and container scanning) tests run in CI and gate merges.
Meet GDPR (and applicable regional privacy law) obligations including data minimisation, lawful basis tracking, retention schedules and breach-notification support. Audit records retained per policy.
UI conforms to WCAG 2.2 AA.
Application is containerised and deployed through a CI/CD pipeline with infrastructure as code, separate dev/test/staging/production environments, and automated rollback.
Supports the latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; internationalisation-ready (UTF-8, locale-aware dates, numbers and translatable strings).
Referential integrity, unique constraints and transactional consistency are enforced in the database; all timestamps stored in UTC.

constraints.description: Backend must be implemented in Java (current LTS version) using an established framework such as Spring Boot.
Frontend must be implemented in React with TypeScript.
PostgreSQL (supported major version) is the primary data store.
Authentication must integrate with the organisation's existing identity provider rather than a bespoke user store.
Only open-source or already-licensed third-party components that pass security and licence review may be used.

assumptions.description: The application is for internal staff use; customers do not log in (no self-service portal).
An enterprise OIDC-compliant identity provider with MFA is available.
Performance and availability targets in NFR-003 and NFR-005 are reasonable defaults pending business sign-off.
The system is the master for customer data and is not initially synchronised with a CRM or ERP, though integration-ready via the API.
Initial release targets a single primary language (English) with a single region of data hosting.
A container platform (e.g. Kubernetes) or managed cloud equivalent and managed PostgreSQL are available.
Expected scale is up to 5 million customer records and about 500 named users.

open_decisions.question: Which backend framework and architecture style should be used?
open_decisions.recommended: Spring Boot modular monolith
open_decisions.impact: Affects delivery speed, operational complexity and team skills; a modular monolith can be split later if needed.

open_decisions.question: What hosting model will be used?
options: Public cloud with managed Kubernetes and managed PostgreSQL
open_decisions.recommended: Public cloud with managed Kubernetes and managed PostgreSQL
open_decisions.impact: Determines IaC tooling, backup/DR design, cost and data residency compliance.

open_decisions.question: How should search be implemented?
open_decisions.recommended: PostgreSQL full-text and trigram indexes
open_decisions.impact: Simpler operations and consistency at expected scale; a search engine adds cost and sync complexity but may be needed if volume or relevance needs grow.

open_decisions.question: Should the system support multi-tenancy?
options: Multi-tenant with shared schema and tenant ID
open_decisions.recommended: Single tenant
open_decisions.impact: Multi-tenancy substantially affects data model, security and testing; retrofitting is costly if later required.

open_decisions.question: What are the data retention and erasure rules for customer and audit data?
options: Retain 7 years after last activity then anonymise
open_decisions.recommended: Retain per jurisdiction-specific schedule
open_decisions.impact: Drives the design of FR-015, audit storage and archival jobs; requires legal input.

open_decisions.question: Which frontend tooling and state/data approach should be used?
options: Vite with React Query and a component library (e.g. MUI)
open_decisions.recommended: Vite with React Query and a component library (e.g. MUI)
open_decisions.impact: Affects build performance, accessibility baseline and hosting; SSR is unnecessary for an authenticated internal app.

open_decisions.question: Are integrations with other systems required in the first release?
open_decisions.recommended: None; API only
open_decisions.impact: Integrations extend scope and need event or messaging design; deferring them keeps the first release focused.

output.title: Enterprise Customer Management Application (Java, React, PostgreSQL)
output.summary: A web-based customer management application for storing, finding, and maintaining customer, contact, and interaction records. The backend is a Java (Spring Boot) REST API, the frontend is a React single-page application, and PostgreSQL is the system of record. It is built to enterprise standards: role-based access control, SSO, audit logging, data protection and privacy compliance, observability, automated testing, CI/CD, and documented operational readiness.

functional_requirements.title: Customer record management
functional_requirements.description: Authorized users can create, view, update, and deactivate customer records (individual or organization) with fields including legal name, display name, type, status, industry, primary email, phone, billing and shipping addresses, tags, and external reference ID.
functional_requirements.acceptance: A user with the Editor role can create, edit, and deactivate a customer; changes persist and appear in the UI and API; required-field and format validation errors are shown inline; deactivated customers are hidden from default lists but retrievable via filter.

functional_requirements.title: Contact management
functional_requirements.description: Each customer can have multiple contacts with name, role, email, phone, and preferred channel; one contact can be flagged as primary.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Contacts can be added, edited, and removed on a customer; exactly one primary contact is enforced per customer; removing a customer's last contact is allowed but warns the user.

functional_requirements.title: Search, filter, sort, and pagination
functional_requirements.description: Users can search customers by name, email, phone, and external ID, filter by status, type, tag, owner, and created/updated date, sort on any list column, and page through results server-side.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Search over 1 million records returns the first page within the performance target; filters combine with AND logic; sort order and page size persist in the URL; partial and case-insensitive matches work.

functional_requirements.title: Interaction and notes log
functional_requirements.description: Users can record notes, calls, meetings, and emails against a customer or contact, with timestamp, author, and type, and view them in a chronological timeline.
functional_requirements.acceptance: A new interaction appears in the timeline immediately with the correct author and time; users can edit or delete only their own entries unless they hold the Manager role; edits are tracked in the audit log.

functional_requirements.title: Customer ownership and assignment
functional_requirements.description: Each customer has an account owner (internal user). Managers can reassign owners individually or in bulk.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Reassignment updates the owner, records an audit entry, and the list can be filtered by owner; bulk reassignment of up to 500 customers completes with a per-record success/failure report.

functional_requirements.title: Authentication and SSO
functional_requirements.description: Users authenticate through the organization's identity provider using OpenID Connect/OAuth 2.0 (with SAML as a possible alternative); the API validates JWT access tokens.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Unauthenticated requests receive 401; users sign in through the IdP; sessions expire after the configured idle time; logout invalidates the session in the application.

functional_requirements.title: Role-based access control
functional_requirements.description: Roles (Admin, Manager, Editor, Viewer) control permissions to view, create, edit, delete, export, reassign, and administer. Authorization is enforced on the server for every endpoint.
functional_requirements.acceptance: A permission matrix is documented and covered by automated tests; a Viewer cannot call write endpoints (403); UI controls are hidden or disabled based on role; role changes take effect within five minutes or at next login.

functional_requirements.title: Audit trail
functional_requirements.description: All create, update, delete, role change, export, and login events are recorded immutably with actor, timestamp, entity, action, and before/after values for changed fields.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Each listed event produces an audit record; Admins and Auditors can search and filter the audit log; audit records cannot be modified or deleted through the application.

functional_requirements.title: Data import and export
functional_requirements.description: Authorized users can import customers from CSV with validation and a preview, and export filtered results to CSV. Exports are permission-controlled and audited.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Import reports row-level errors without partial silent failure and supports an all-or-nothing option; duplicate detection runs on import; export honors the current filters and the user's field-level permissions; each export creates an audit entry.

functional_requirements.title: Duplicate detection and merge
functional_requirements.description: The system flags potential duplicate customers on create and on demand (by normalized name, email, phone, and address) and lets Managers merge two records while retaining history.
functional_requirements.acceptance: A likely duplicate triggers a warning at creation that the user can override; merging combines contacts and interactions into the surviving record, and the merged record is retained as an alias and audited.

functional_requirements.title: Privacy and data subject requests
functional_requirements.description: Support retrieval, correction, export, and erasure or anonymization of an individual's personal data to satisfy GDPR/CCPA-style requests, with retention rules.
functional_requirements.acceptance: An Admin can locate all data for a person, export it in a machine-readable format, and anonymize it; anonymization is irreversible, preserves referential integrity, and leaves an audit entry without the personal data.

functional_requirements.title: Dashboard and basic reporting
functional_requirements.description: A landing dashboard shows counts of customers by status, recent activity, and customers created over time; users can save filtered list views.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Dashboard figures match database counts at load time and respect the user's data access scope; saved views are private to the user unless shared.

functional_requirements.title: REST API and documentation
functional_requirements.description: The backend exposes a versioned REST API documented with OpenAPI, using consistent error formats, validation, and idempotent updates with optimistic locking.
functional_requirements.acceptance: An OpenAPI spec is generated and published at build time; concurrent edits to the same record return 409 rather than overwrite; all errors follow one documented schema.

functional_requirements.title: Administration
functional_requirements.description: Admins can manage users' roles, configurable picklists (status, type, tags, industries), and system settings.
functional_requirements.acceptance: Picklist changes appear in the UI without redeployment; changes are audited; values in use cannot be hard-deleted, only retired.
